correctness.rationale: For fixed (u,K), six independent tensor-coordinate conditions give a P^29 fiber and a 34-dimensional incidence. For two distinct points u,u', the two six-condition blocks occupy independent U-slices, so the double-incidence locus has dimension 10+(36-12-1)=33. Rank zero at one point gives dimension at most 3+(36-9-1)+2=31. Both are proper subsets of the 34-dimensional incidence, so the general fiber has one rank-one point and one kernel. Combined with Sherratt's irreducible image and generic finiteness, the projection is birational. The projective-bundle source is rational.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary paper proves that the incidence projects generically finitely onto an irreducible degree-24 divisor but does not state generic degree one or rationality. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches for the rank-one tensor divisor, its incidence model, and rationality found no equivalent or stronger statement. The new dimension-33 double-incidence and dimension-31 rank-zero exclusions are not consequences of generic finiteness alone.

value.rationale: This gives a global birational model and generic-uniqueness theorem for a newly highlighted degree-24 invariant divisor. It advances the structural geometry of the boundary locus beyond its known degree and irreducibility and provides a concrete rational parametrization useful for studying its singularities and quotient geometry.
